subject: Escalation: Acme Health — request for partial termination + staged ramp protections
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: request to add partial termination & staged ramp — need approval

Hi Laura / Karthik,

Quick summary from the Acme procurement call this morning: they want the option to reduce committed capacity (a partial termination / "downsized commitment") after the initial 90-day onboarding window. Their ask includes: a staged ramp schedule (allowing X% reduction in quarter 1, more later), an opt-out/termination for convenience after 12 months, and protection against large penalties.

Customer rationale: regulatory budgeting uncertainty and phased rollout across product lines. They are committed to an initial 12-month term and immediate production usage, but want flexibility to scale down without a full early termination penalty. Pricing ask: reduce monthly committed minimum by up to 40% in month 4 with notification.

Attached is their redline (Acme_Health_Redline_v3.docx). From a commercial perspective the logo/expansion upside is large but the ask is non-standard. Can we get deal desk/legal/exec guidance on acceptable guardrails (downsell protections, minimum revenue floors, notice windows, termination fees) so I can respond today?

Proposed quick compromises from my side:
- 90-day onboarding minimum where no reductions allowed
- After 90 days, allow an initial 20% voluntary ramp-down with 60 days' notice
- Any further reductions require quarterly steps of no more than 10% with a defined break fee (e.g., pro-rated commitment or 50% of remaining committed value)

If we need exec sign-off for any deviation from standard termination/commitment language, please escalate.

Thanks,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: request to add partial termination & staged ramp — need approval

Karthik / Vivek — looping you both in.

Marissa captured the ask accurately. High-level assessment: the customer is asking for a mix of a convenience termination after 12 months and a multi-step downsize path that erodes committed revenue risk. We should avoid a blanket convenience termination in year 1; we can offer a controlled "staged downsizing" with clear floors and a termination mechanic tied to remaining committed value.

Suggested executive decision items (so we can give Acme a single answer):
1) Maximum initial downsizing allowed at first eligible date (I recommend 25%).
2) Notice window (60 days seems reasonable).
3) A minimum revenue floor for the full 12-month term (e.g., 70% of committed ARR billed and non-cancellable for first 12 months).
4) Early termination fee if they choose the convenience termination at month 12: equal to remaining committed value * 50%, or allow credits if they commit to a new scaled baseline.

This is borderline for a standard playbook exception; Vivek, do we want to authorize a one-time deviation on thresholds and fee formula for Acme? If so, I propose we approve conditionally and require the customer sign the attached limited-scope amendment and DocuSign routing through legal.

Thanks,
Laura
--
Laura Bennett
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: request to add partial termination & staged ramp — need approval

Laura / Marissa — legal input and suggested draft language below. I redlined the customer's doc and recommend we offer a controlled amendment rather than a freeform convenience termination. Key legal points:

- "Staged Downsizing" definition: Customer may reduce the committed capacity by no more than 25% at the first eligible reduction date (which shall be 90 days after the Effective Date) upon providing 60 days' advance written notice to Redwood.
- Subsequent reductions: Customer may request further reductions not to exceed 10% of the original commitment per quarter thereafter, subject to 60 days' notice and mutual written agreement.
- Revenue floor and billing: Customer remains liable for a minimum of 70% of the annual committed amount for the first 12 months (the "Minimum Commitment").
- Early Termination at Month 12: Customer may terminate for convenience at or after the 12-month anniversary upon payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the remaining committed value, unless the parties agree to a replacement commitment in writing.

If the execs are comfortable with those numeric thresholds (25% initial / 10% quarterly / 70% floor / 50% fee), legal can finalize the amendment and prepare DocuSign. If not, propose alternatives and we'll re-draft quickly.

-Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme: request to add partial termination & staged ramp — need approval

Thanks for the thorough breakdown. I support a controlled exception for Acme given strategic value and potential expansion across their lines. Approve the following conditional terms:

1) Initial eligible downsizing after 90 days: up to 25% with 60 days' notice.
2) Subsequent reductions: up to 10% of original commitment per quarter, documented by amendment.
3) Minimum revenue floor for first 12 months: 70% of committed ARR (billed as scheduled).
4) Convenience termination on or after 12-month anniversary: allowed subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of remaining committed value.

Conditions: All changes must be captured in a single signed amendment and routed via DocuSign. Any deviation from the numeric thresholds above requires VP-level approval. Also require that any reduction that would drop committed revenue below 50% of original commitment must be escalated to me first.

Approve and ask legal to prepare the amendment for signature. Laura/Marissa, proceed to offer these terms to Acme and attach the amendment for signature.

—Vivek

- Initial downsizing allowed after 90 days: up to 25% reduction with 60 days' prior written notice.
- Subsequent reductions: up to 10% of the original commitment per quarter, with 60 days' notice and a short amendment.
- 12-month minimum revenue floor: Customer remains liable for 70% of the annual committed amount for the first 12 months.
- Convenience termination: allowed on or after the 12-month anniversary upon payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the remaining committed value.
